project.title: Plant Disease Classifier Reliability Study
project.short_description: A pre-registered study of what happens when plant-disease classifiers that score about 99% on PlantVillage meet field photos from PlantDoc. Accuracy fell to 14–17%, and the models stayed confidently wrong.
project.overview: Plant-disease classifiers often report about 99% accuracy on the PlantVillage benchmark, whose photos are leaves on plain backgrounds. This project asks what happens when the same models see field-style photos from PlantDoc, and whether their confidence can be trusted to say “I don’t know.” I trained a from-scratch CNN and a fine-tuned ImageNet ResNet-18 on PlantVillage, tested them once on PlantDoc, and measured the accuracy gap, calibration and abstention. The protocol, splits and decisions were fixed in public commits before the external data was used.
project.problem_statement: A model that scores 99% on a clean benchmark can fail on real field images, and a wrong answer given with high confidence is worse than no answer. Two things were measured: how much accuracy is lost under the shift, and whether the model’s confidence warns us when it is wrong enough to support abstaining.
project.dataset_info:
• Source: PlantVillage colour images, with 23 classes shared with the external set.
  • Splits: the data was split by leaf (70% train, 7.5% model selection, 7.5% calibration, 15% test), so the same leaf never appears in two splits. Checks found zero group or hash overlap across splits and with the external set.
  • External: PlantDoc, de-duplicated and mapped to PlantVillage classes, giving 1,993 images with at least 53 per class. It was never used for training, tuning, calibration or thresholds.
  • Data integrity: the files were verified against SHA-256 manifests (35,410 files).
  • Licence note: PlantDoc is CC BY 4.0. I couldn’t confirm the PlantVillage licence, so datasets and trained weights are not redistributed.
project.methodology:
• Pre-registered protocol: hypotheses, metrics and decision rules were written before any external evaluation.
  • Two models, three seeds each: a 3.4M-parameter scratch CNN and ResNet-18 (11.2M parameters), reported individually.
  • Source-only calibration: one temperature per run, fitted on the calibration split.
  • Abstention rules: two thresholds chosen on the calibration split, one keeping 90% coverage and one capping risk at 1%.
  • Frozen decisions: each run’s temperature, thresholds and checkpoint hash were committed before any external inference, and the evaluator refuses to run if verification fails.
  • Statistics: 10,000-resample cluster bootstrap for intervals, gap and paired model comparisons.
  • Metrics: accuracy, macro-F1, ECE, Brier score, NLL, AURC and AUROC for error detection.
project.implementation_details:
• PyTorch and torchvision on a Colab T4 GPU, about 17 minutes per run.
  • AdamW, mixed precision, a cosine learning-rate schedule with warmup, GPU-side augmentation, and checkpoints chosen by lowest validation loss.
  • Learning rates chosen from three values per model on selection data only.
  • 229 automated tests covering metrics, bootstrap, checkpointing, the freeze verifier and the training loop.
  • Results, tables and figures regenerate from the repo, and the project page is hosted on GitHub Pages with interactive abstention and calibration plots.
project.results:
• Accuracy collapse: PlantVillage test accuracy was 0.987–0.988 (CNN) and 0.994–0.996 (ResNet-18). On PlantDoc it was 0.143–0.154 and 0.149–0.167 respectively, against 0.043 chance. The gap is about 83 percentage points for both, with 95% intervals of roughly 81–86.
  • Pretrained against scratch: ResNet-18 scored higher in all three seeds, but the paired interval excluded zero in only one, so the advantage is not demonstrated under the pre-set rule.
  • Calibration: ECE on PlantDoc was 0.58–0.74, against 0.003–0.005 on the PlantVillage test. Temperature scaling fitted on source data slightly worsened the external result.
  • Abstention: confidence separated right from wrong answers weakly on PlantDoc (AUROC 0.59–0.63) compared with 0.97–0.99 on the source. The 90%-coverage rule accepted only 8–19% of PlantDoc images, at a 63–78% error rate.
project.future_improvements:
• Have a plant pathologist review the class mapping.
  • Test whether a small labelled field sample fixes calibration and abstention, kept separate from the evaluation set.
  • Repeat the study with more architectures, other datasets and a second split seed.
  • Try domain-robust training such as stronger augmentation or background removal.
  • Add a walkthrough video.
project.my_role: I defined the research question, the evaluation rules and the standards of honesty for the project, the code, experiments and were reviewed every decision and result.
project.key_learnings:
• Benchmark accuracy says little about performance under a changed image style.
  • Calibration fitted on the source domain does not transfer, and a negative result reported carefully is more useful than a flattering one.
  • Preventing leakage, using each test set once and freezing decisions before looking at the data are practical habits that make results trustworthy.
  • I also learned to state what the data does not support, such as the pretrained model’s advantage.
